citation.title: Interpolation-Prediction Networks for Irregularly Sampled Time Series
citation.authors: S. N. Shukla, B. M. Marlin

topic: Supervised learning from sparse, irregular, unaligned multivariate time series using RBF interpolation layers followed by a GRU
own_question: Can semi-parametric interpolation onto a regular reference grid, with cross-channel sharing and an observation-intensity channel, support end-to-end classification and regression on sparse clinical series?
actual_method_and_evidence: The method uses RBF smooth and high-pass interpolants, an intensity channel (sum of kernel weights), and learned cross-channel correlations. The interpolants feed a GRU. Training combines a supervised loss with a masked held-out-point reconstruction loss. Evidence comes from MIMIC-III mortality and length-of-stay prediction using 5-fold CV over a fixed 48 h window, and from a subsampled UWave dataset. Reported results are better mean metrics than GRU-D variants and GP-GRU, and comparable UWave accuracy to a GP adapter with reported faster training. The ablation finds the intensity channel informative. The kernels are two-sided over the whole window, so the interpolation is offline and noncausal.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Prior ML work maps irregular, unaligned multichannel observations onto a regular grid via learned kernel interpolation, sharing information across channels and encoding observation timing as an intensity channel.
claim_checks.qualification: The interpolation is two-sided over a fixed window, not causal nowcasting. It was applied to clinical and gesture data, not plasma diagnostics.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Masked reconstruction of held-out observations has been used to prevent kernel interpolators from trivially fitting their inputs.
claim_checks.qualification: This is a training-signal design, not evidence for CES label validity.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Inputs are a full 48 h window of observations. The target is an outcome observed after that window. No streaming, causal, or arrival-time setting is studied.
validation_if_relevant: MIMIC-III uses 5-fold CV with early stopping on validation drawn from the training folds. UWave uses a standard train/test split. The study does not address temporal, leakage-aware, or campaign-level splits.
forbidden_inferences: That this method is causal or suitable for real-time use
That it validates our 10 ms timing or our use of BES/ECEI inputs
That its MIMIC gains transfer to KSTAR CES nowcasting
That two-sided interpolation baselines are equivalent to its model
That intensity-channel usefulness implies a plasma physical mechanism
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Include as background on irregular-sampling representation (cross-channel interpolation and an observation-timing channel). Contrast it explicitly with our strictly-past causal setting. Do not treat it as a performance benchmark.
